stride.title: Unauthenticated colleague requests could be accepted as another colleague
stride.description: `flow:colleague-to-scheduling-web-app:view-shifts` crosses from the public internet to `process:scheduling-web-app` with `authentication: unknown`. If that unknown resolves to no verified caller identity, an internet attacker can impersonate `entity:colleague` and request shifts as a chosen colleague. Second-order: `process:scheduling-web-app` forwards rota reads to `process:scheduling-service`, which reads colleague names, contact details, availability, and rota data from `store:rota-database`. This is conditional on the undocumented authentication attribute, not an assertion that authentication is absent.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unknown authentication value, because `flow:colleague-to-scheduling-web-app:view-shifts` is a crossing from `boundary:public-internet` to the internet-facing `process:scheduling-web-app`, allowing any internet user to attempt the request. Impact is medium because the flow and `process:scheduling-web-app` handle PII and the impersonated read can reach colleague details held in `store:rota-database`.

mitigations.summary: Document and enforce verified colleague identity on the public flow
mitigations.detail: Set explicit, verifiable authentication for `flow:colleague-to-scheduling-web-app:view-shifts`, such as OIDC with short-lived sessions, and bind every rota-read authorization decision to the authenticated colleague identity rather than a caller-supplied identifier.

mitigations.summary: Use phishing-resistant human authentication
mitigations.detail: Require WebAuthn/passkeys for colleague sessions that access rota and contact information, with breached-password screening and rate limits if passwords remain supported.

stride.title: Unauthenticated manager requests could let an attacker alter a store rota
stride.description: `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota` crosses from the public internet into `process:scheduling-web-app` with `authentication: unknown`. If the undocumented authentication control does not verify the manager identity, an internet attacker can impersonate `entity:store-manager` and submit rota changes for a store. Second-order: the web app sends those reads and writes to `process:scheduling-service`, which writes rota and colleague-detail records in `store:rota-database`; altered rotas also feed the weekly payroll export. This is conditional on the unknown authentication value.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unknown authentication value, because this is a public-internet boundary crossing into internet-facing `process:scheduling-web-app` and an attacker can directly submit manager-style requests. Impact is high because the flow writes `business-critical-data` and PII, reaches the rota database through `process:scheduling-service`, and can affect the payroll export.

mitigations.summary: Require strongly authenticated manager sessions
mitigations.detail: Make `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota` use explicit OIDC authentication with phishing-resistant WebAuthn/passkey MFA and short-lived, protected sessions.

mitigations.summary: Bind store authority to the verified manager identity
mitigations.detail: Have `process:scheduling-web-app` and `process:scheduling-service` enforce that each rota write is authorized for the store in a verified identity claim, not a store identifier supplied in the request.

stride.title: A compromised internal host could impersonate the web app to the scheduling service
stride.description: `flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests` remains within `boundary:internal-network`, but its `authentication` is unknown. If the scheduling service accepts requests based only on internal reachability, an attacker with a foothold on that network can impersonate `process:scheduling-web-app` to `process:scheduling-service` and issue rota reads or writes. Second-order: `process:scheduling-service` has read-write paths to `store:rota-database` and writes the weekly payroll export to `store:file-share`, so the forged service requests reach business-critical rota data, colleague PII, and payroll data. This is conditional on the unverified authentication attribute.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication value: exploitation requires an internal-network foothold, but the model provides no verified identity control for `flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests`. Impact is high because `process:scheduling-service` handles PII and `business-critical-data`, reads and writes `store:rota-database`, and writes payroll exports.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate service-to-service requests independent of network location
mitigations.detail: Use mTLS or workload-identity-issued, audience-bound short-lived tokens on `flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests`, and make `process:scheduling-service` reject unauthenticated callers.

mitigations.summary: Authorize the web-app workload identity narrowly
mitigations.detail: Give the scheduling web app a distinct workload identity and permit it only the rota operations it requires, rather than treating all internal-network origins as the same caller.

stride.title: An attacker could impersonate the payroll system to collect payroll exports
stride.description: `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export` crosses from `boundary:payroll-team-environment` into `store:file-share` on the internal network with `authentication: unknown`. If the file share does not verify a payroll-specific machine identity, an attacker able to originate from that external environment can impersonate `entity:payroll-system` and collect the weekly payroll export. The export is written by `process:scheduling-service` and carries PII, so the impersonation exposes payroll data beyond the file-share endpoint. This is conditional on the undocumented authentication control.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication value: the attacker must be able to originate from `boundary:payroll-team-environment`, but no verified caller identity is documented on this boundary crossing. Impact is medium because the collected weekly payroll export and `store:file-share` are tagged PII.

mitigations.summary: Give the payroll system a unique verified machine identity
mitigations.detail: Require mTLS with a payroll-system-specific certificate, or short-lived audience-bound workload tokens, for `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export`; do not authorize collection based on network origin alone.

mitigations.summary: Restrict and audit export retrieval
mitigations.detail: Allow the verified payroll identity to read only its intended export objects and record each retrieval against that distinct identity.

stride.title: A fake scheduling web app could impersonate the service endpoint to public users
stride.description: Both public flows to `process:scheduling-web-app` have `protocol: unknown` and `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If those unknowns resolve to missing TLS with certificate validation, an on-path attacker can impersonate `process:scheduling-web-app` to `entity:colleague` or `entity:store-manager` over `flow:colleague-to-scheduling-web-app:view-shifts` or `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota`. The fake endpoint can elicit whatever authentication material or rota requests users send; successful impersonation of a manager-facing interaction can then be used to change business-critical rota data through the real application. This is conditional on the undocumented protocol and transport-authenticity controls.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown transport controls: both flows cross from the public internet, but endpoint substitution requires an on-path or equivalent routing position. Impact is high because the manager flow carries PII and business-critical rota writes, which reach `process:scheduling-service` and `store:rota-database`.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated TLS for every public web-app connection
mitigations.detail: Use TLS 1.2+ with full certificate-chain and hostname validation for both public flows to `process:scheduling-web-app`, and document the resulting protocol and encryption-in-transit attributes.

mitigations.summary: Protect sessions from endpoint and transport theft
mitigations.detail: Use secure, HttpOnly, SameSite session cookies or short-lived tokens only over validated HTTPS, and require reauthentication for sensitive rota changes.

stride.title: Rota changes can be modified in transit if manager traffic lacks verified integrity protection
stride.description: `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `process:scheduling-web-app`, but its `protocol`, `authentication`, and `encryption_in_transit` are all unknown. If the unverified transport protection does not provide authenticated integrity, an on-path attacker can alter a manager's rota entries before `process:scheduling-web-app` receives them. The altered request can then be forwarded through `flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests` and persisted by `process:scheduling-service` through `flow:scheduling-service-to-rota-database:read-write-rotas`, changing authoritative rota and availability information in `store:rota-database`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium, conditional on the unknown transport and authentication attributes of the internet-to-internal crossing `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota`; an attacker still needs an on-path position. Impact is high because the modified request can be persisted in `store:rota-database`, which holds PII and is tagged `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Verify and require authenticated TLS for manager-to-app traffic
mitigations.detail: Document and enforce TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation on `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota`, ensuring integrity protection rather than merely network reachability.

mitigations.summary: Authorize and validate rota mutations at the service
mitigations.detail: Have `process:scheduling-service` authenticate the originating manager context, enforce store ownership, and apply server-side allowlist validation to rota writes before persistence.

stride.title: Direct modification of rota records is possible if the service-to-database write identity is not enforced
stride.description: `flow:scheduling-service-to-rota-database:read-write-rotas` performs read-write operations on `store:rota-database`, but the flow's `authentication` is unknown. If this unknown resolves to absent or ineffective database write authentication, an attacker with access to the internal database path can alter rota entries, colleague contact details, or stated availability directly rather than through `process:scheduling-service`. This bypasses the service's intended write path; later rota reads through `process:scheduling-service` and `process:scheduling-web-app` will treat the corrupted records as authoritative.

grounds.text: Nobody has documented how colleagues or managers sign in, how the web app and the scheduling service identify each other, how the payroll system is identified when it collects the export, or whether any of it is encrypted.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:flow:scheduling-service-to-rota-database:read-write-rotas:authentication`: the database is on the internal network, so an attacker needs internal-path access, but no write identity control is verified. Impact is high because `store:rota-database` contains colleague PII and business-critical rota data that downstream application reads trust.

mitigations.summary: Enforce authenticated least-privilege database access
mitigations.detail: Require a dedicated authenticated workload identity for `process:scheduling-service` on `flow:scheduling-service-to-rota-database:read-write-rotas`, deny anonymous access, and grant only the required statements and tables.

mitigations.summary: Protect the database connection integrity
mitigations.detail: Use mutually authenticated TLS on the service-to-database flow and restrict database network access to the scheduling service identity.

mitigations.summary: Detect unauthorized rota changes
mitigations.detail: Maintain versioned, integrity-protected change history for rota and colleague records and reconcile changes against authorized service actions.

stride.title: Payroll exports can be replaced if writes to the file share are not authenticated
stride.description: `flow:scheduling-service-to-file-share:write-payroll-export` writes the weekly payroll export to `store:file-share`, while its `authentication` is unknown. If the file share does not enforce a distinct authenticated, authorized writer identity, an attacker who reaches the internal share can plant or replace a payroll export with altered pay-related records. `entity:payroll-system` subsequently collects the file through `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export` and may consume the attacker-supplied file as the weekly export, extending the integrity failure into payroll processing.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication on `flow:scheduling-service-to-file-share:write-payroll-export`; the attacker needs access to the internal file-share path, but no verified writer identity is stated. Impact is medium because a forged weekly payroll export containing PII can be collected across the `boundary:payroll-team-environment` crossing and affect payroll processing.

mitigations.summary: Restrict payroll-export writes to the scheduling service identity
mitigations.detail: Require authenticated, least-privilege access on `store:file-share`, with a writer principal used only by `process:scheduling-service` and a separate read-only principal for `entity:payroll-system`.

mitigations.summary: Sign exports and verify them before payroll ingestion
mitigations.detail: Have `process:scheduling-service` sign each versioned export and require the payroll system to verify the signature, expected producer, and freshness before processing.

mitigations.summary: Protect collection traffic with authenticated transport
mitigations.detail: Establish mTLS or equivalent authenticated encryption for `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export` so collection requests and export responses cannot be modified across the payroll-team boundary.

stride.title: Rota changes may be deniable because the model cannot bind them to a manager
stride.description: A store manager using `entity:store-manager` can change rota entries through `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota`, which crosses from `boundary:public-internet` into `process:scheduling-web-app`. Authentication on that flow, on `flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests`, and on the service write path `flow:scheduling-service-to-rota-database:read-write-rotas` is unknown. If these paths do not establish and propagate an individual manager identity into an immutable security-event record, a manager can alter a rota in `store:rota-database` and later deny making the change; the current rota state cannot rebut them. The model also contains no audit log element or audit flow for these business-critical writes, so it cannot demonstrate that before/after values, actor, timestamp, and outcome are retained. Second-order, disputed shift assignments and availability changes affecting the rota corpus cannot be resolved reliably.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unknown authentication attributes: `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota` is a boundary crossing from `boundary:public-internet`, and an ordinary manager is already positioned to dispute their own rota changes. Impact is medium because `store:rota-database` holds `pii` and `business-critical-data`, so inability to establish responsibility affects operationally important rota decisions across the store.

mitigations.summary: Use individual manager identities and preserve the originating subject across service hops
mitigations.detail: Establish per-manager authentication on `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota` and propagate the verified subject through `process:scheduling-web-app` and `process:scheduling-service`; record both the originating manager and service identity for each write.

mitigations.summary: Create an immutable rota change trail
mitigations.detail: Have `process:scheduling-service` emit structured events for rota writes to a dedicated append-only audit store, including actor, action, affected rota entry, before/after values, timestamp, request identifier, and outcome. Make corrections new records rather than overwrites.

stride.title: Payroll-system collection of weekly exports may be externally deniable
stride.description: `entity:payroll-system`, operated from `boundary:payroll-team-environment`, initiates collection of the weekly export from `store:file-share` through the boundary-crossing `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export`. Its authentication is unknown. If the collection request is not individually authenticated and signed, neither team can produce durable evidence that this payroll system requested or received a particular export, allowing the external team to deny a disputed collection or delivery. The model contains no audit log element or flow recording collection events; consequently, the payroll export written through `flow:scheduling-service-to-file-share:write-payroll-export` may lack a defensible delivery history. This is conditional on resolving the unknown authentication control and audit arrangement.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown authentication on `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export`: the flow crosses from the separately operated `boundary:payroll-team-environment`, but a disputed collection requires a partner-side event or a caller able to use an unverified path. Impact is medium because `store:file-share` holds payroll exports tagged `pii`, and an unresolved delivery dispute can affect payroll processing and the accountability of both teams.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and sign payroll-export collection requests
mitigations.detail: Use a distinct payroll-system identity on `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export` and retain timestamped, nonce-protected signed requests or receipts for the dispute-retention period.

mitigations.summary: Record immutable export delivery events
mitigations.detail: Record export creation and collection events with the export identifier or digest, authenticated payroll-system identity, timestamp, request identifier, and outcome in a dedicated append-only audit store outside the ordinary file-share write authority.

stride.title: Colleague shift responses may be readable across the public-internet boundary
stride.description: `flow:colleague-to-scheduling-web-app:view-shifts` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `process:scheduling-web-app`, carries PII, and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If transport encryption is not enforced for the request and its same-interaction response, an attacker able to observe the colleague's network path can intercept that colleague's shifts. The disclosure reveals work patterns that can be used to target the colleague through the public-facing application; this is conditional on verifying the transport protection.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses `boundary:public-internet` but interception requires an on-path position, while `unknown:flow:colleague-to-scheduling-web-app:view-shifts:encryption_in_transit` provides no verified transport control. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII concerning a colleague's shifts.

mitigations.summary: Verify and require TLS for colleague access
mitigations.detail: Set and enforce TLS 1.2+ for `flow:colleague-to-scheduling-web-app:view-shifts`, including the response carrying shift information; reject insecure HTTP and downgrade attempts.

stride.title: Store rota data may be readable on manager traffic from the public internet
stride.description: `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `process:scheduling-web-app`, carries rota entries with PII and business-critical data, and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If this unknown resolves to unencrypted or improperly terminated transport, an on-path attacker can intercept a manager's store rota entries while they are created or changed. The exposed rota and colleague context can then be used to target colleagues and to learn operational staffing information; this is conditional on the unverified transport setting.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional: `crossing:flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota` exposes the path to public-network observers, but they still need an on-path position and encryption is unverified by `unknown:flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota:encryption_in_transit`. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII and business-critical rota data.

mitigations.summary: Require TLS for all manager-to-app traffic
mitigations.detail: Enforce modern TLS and HSTS on `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota`; ensure TLS termination and any onward hop are documented and protected.

stride.title: Rota requests may be readable on the unverified app-to-service hop
stride.description: `flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests` carries PII and business-critical rota reads and writes, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the internal hop is not encrypted, an attacker with a foothold able to observe `boundary:internal-network` can intercept requests and returned rota data between `process:scheduling-web-app` and `process:scheduling-service`. The information identifies rota operations that the scheduling service subsequently performs against `store:rota-database`, enabling targeted follow-on attacks; this is conditional on the unknown transport control.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `unknown:flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests:encryption_in_transit` leaves protection unverified, but observing this intra-`boundary:internal-network` flow requires a prior internal foothold. Impact is medium because the flow carries PII and business-critical rota data.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate the service hop
mitigations.detail: Use TLS 1.2+ with mTLS between `process:scheduling-web-app` and `process:scheduling-service`, and record the resulting `encryption_in_transit` and authentication settings on the flow.

stride.title: Colleague contact and availability records may be readable on the database connection
stride.description: `flow:scheduling-service-to-rota-database:read-write-rotas` carries rota entries, colleague names, contact details, and stated availability, while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the database connection is plaintext, an attacker able to observe the internal path can intercept these records as `process:scheduling-service` reads or writes `store:rota-database`. The attacker gains personal contact and availability information that can be used for targeted social engineering, without needing to query the database directly; this is conditional on the unverified encryption state.

grounds.text: Colleague names, contact details and stated availability are held in that database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `unknown:flow:scheduling-service-to-rota-database:read-write-rotas:encryption_in_transit` is unverified but an attacker must first obtain an internal-path observation position. Impact is medium because the flow carries colleague PII, including contact details and availability.

mitigations.summary: Require encrypted database transport
mitigations.detail: Configure authenticated TLS for `flow:scheduling-service-to-rota-database:read-write-rotas` and require certificate validation rather than treating the internal network as a trusted channel.

stride.title: Weekly payroll exports may be readable on the internal write path
stride.description: `flow:scheduling-service-to-file-share:write-payroll-export` carries the weekly payroll export to `store:file-share` with `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If the file-share protocol or its transport is unencrypted, an attacker with internal network visibility can intercept each weekly export as `process:scheduling-service` writes it. The captured PII can be used to target colleagues and remains available to the attacker after the export has been collected; this is conditional on verifying the transport setting.

grounds.text: Once a week the scheduling service writes a payroll export onto a file share.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `unknown:flow:scheduling-service-to-file-share:write-payroll-export:encryption_in_transit` leaves the control unverified, while interception of this internal flow requires a prior foothold. Impact is medium because the export flow carries PII.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the payroll-export write hop
mitigations.detail: Use a file-sharing protocol protected by TLS or equivalent transport encryption for `flow:scheduling-service-to-file-share:write-payroll-export`, with authenticated service identities.

stride.title: Payroll exports may be readable while collected by the external payroll environment
stride.description: `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export` crosses from `boundary:payroll-team-environment` into `boundary:internal-network`, carries PII, and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If this collection channel lacks verified encryption, an attacker able to observe the cross-environment route can intercept the weekly payroll export. The data can be retained and used to target colleagues after the collection transaction, so this is not limited to a transient operational exposure; the threat is conditional on the unknown transport setting.

grounds.text: The payroll system, which is run by another team, collects the export from the file share.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional: the collection crosses between `boundary:payroll-team-environment` and `boundary:internal-network`, while `unknown:flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export:encryption_in_transit` provides no verified protection; interception still requires access to that path. Impact is medium because the collected export carries PII.

mitigations.summary: Use mutually authenticated encrypted collection
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ with mTLS or an equivalently authenticated encrypted transfer mechanism for `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export`.

stride.title: A copied rota-database volume may expose colleague records if encryption at rest is absent
stride.description: `store:rota-database` holds rota information plus colleague names, contact details, and stated availability, is tagged PII, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If this unknown resolves to no effective at-rest encryption, an attacker or over-privileged storage operator obtaining the database media or an operational copy can read the records without using `process:scheduling-service` or its database access path. The disclosure supplies contact and availability data usable for targeted attacks against colleagues; this claim is conditional and does not assert that the database is unencrypted.

grounds.text: Colleague names, contact details and stated availability are held in that database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `unknown:store:rota-database:encryption_at_rest` leaves storage-layer protection unverified; a copied volume or operational copy avoids the normal application path but must first be obtained. Impact is medium because the store holds PII including contact details and availability.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for the rota database
mitigations.detail: Establish the `encryption_at_rest` posture for `store:rota-database`, then use managed envelope encryption with restricted key access and explicitly cover backups, snapshots, replicas, and decommissioned media.

stride.title: The payroll export may be readable by unauthorized collectors if share authentication is absent or overly broad
stride.description: `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export` is a cross-boundary read path to `store:file-share`, carries PII, and has `authentication: unknown`. If the file share does not enforce a dedicated, least-privilege payroll identity and authorization for the specific export, an attacker or another over-privileged principal in `boundary:payroll-team-environment` can read the weekly payroll export. The attacker obtains colleague payroll-related PII and can retain it outside the scheduling system; this is conditional on resolving the unknown authentication and authorization design.

grounds.text: Nobody has documented ... how the payroll system is identified when it collects the export

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the read flow crosses from `boundary:payroll-team-environment` and `unknown:flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export:authentication` leaves collector identity unverified, although the attacker needs access to that environment or path. Impact is medium because `store:file-share` and the read flow carry PII.

mitigations.summary: Enforce a dedicated least-privilege payroll reader identity
mitigations.detail: Require strong service authentication for `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export`, authorize only the intended payroll principal to read only its required export, and deny listing or access to other share content.

mitigations.summary: Audit export reads without logging export contents
mitigations.detail: Record the authenticated collector, export identifier, and access time for `store:file-share`, while redacting payroll data from telemetry.

stride.title: Internet request flooding can exhaust the scheduling web app and rota path
stride.description: An internet-based attacker can flood `process:scheduling-web-app` through `flow:colleague-to-scheduling-web-app:view-shifts` and `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota`. Authentication on both boundary-crossing flows is `unknown`, so it is unverified whether the app rejects anonymous traffic before it performs work or whether request, concurrency, and timeout limits protect it. Each accepted view or rota-change request is forwarded over `flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests` for rota reads or writes, allowing cheap repeated requests to consume the web app's workers/connections and propagate load to `process:scheduling-service` and ultimately the rota database. Second-order, colleagues cannot view assigned shifts and managers cannot build or amend store rotas while the shared public-facing app or its downstream service is saturated.

grounds.text: Store managers use a scheduling web app to build the weekly rota for their store. Colleagues use the same app to look at the shifts they have been given.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditionally on the unverified authentication posture: both attacker-originated flows cross from `boundary:public-internet` and their `authentication` attributes are `unknown`, so broad external request generation has no stated hard prerequisite. Impact is medium because the one shared `process:scheduling-web-app` serves both colleague shift viewing and manager rota creation, and saturation also reaches `process:scheduling-service`; the model does not tag either element as `availability-critical`.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and meter public requests before downstream rota work
mitigations.detail: Establish and enforce authentication for both public flows, then apply per-verified-user and per-source rate, concurrency, and cost limits at `process:scheduling-web-app` before forwarding requests to `process:scheduling-service`.

mitigations.summary: Bound request and dependency consumption
mitigations.detail: Set request-size limits, aggressive read/idle timeouts, bounded worker and downstream-connection pools, and fail-fast load shedding on the web-app-to-service rota path so excess traffic does not queue indefinitely.

mitigations.summary: Isolate downstream failure
mitigations.detail: Use timeouts, circuit breaking, and bounded retries on `flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests` to prevent a saturated scheduling service or rota database from holding all web-app request capacity.

stride.title: Repeated payroll-export collection may starve the shared file share
stride.description: If `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export` accepts requests without effective identity checks or connection/rate bounds, an attacker able to act from `boundary:payroll-team-environment` can repeatedly initiate collection requests against `store:file-share`. The flow's authentication and protocol are `unknown`, so the available controls and the file share's connection and throughput limits are unverified. Repeated reads can consume the file share's finite I/O, connection, or request capacity at lower cost than the share and payroll-export path expend serving them. Second-order, `process:scheduling-service` may be unable to complete its weekly write on `flow:scheduling-service-to-file-share:write-payroll-export`, delaying payroll processing even though the scheduling service itself was not directly flooded.

grounds.text: Once a week the scheduling service writes a payroll export onto a file share. The payroll system, which is run by another team, collects the export from the file share.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on unknown controls: the collection flow crosses from the separately operated `boundary:payroll-team-environment`, but exploiting it requires the attacker to obtain a position in that environment or access to its collection path; its authentication is `unknown`. Impact is medium because `store:file-share` is shared by payroll collection and the scheduling service's weekly payroll-export write, so saturation can delay the operational payroll flow, though the model does not establish an availability-critical tag or irreversible harm.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and authorize payroll collection requests
mitigations.detail: Resolve the `authentication` unknown on `flow:payroll-system-to-file-share:collect-payroll-export` and require a dedicated payroll-system identity with authorization limited to the intended export.

mitigations.summary: Protect file-share capacity from collection bursts
mitigations.detail: Apply per-client connection and request limits, short idle/read timeouts, bounded concurrency, and load shedding on collection access to `store:file-share` so read floods cannot consume capacity needed for `process:scheduling-service` writes.

mitigations.summary: Reserve or separate export-write capacity
mitigations.detail: Use separate quotas or bulkheads for `flow:scheduling-service-to-file-share:write-payroll-export` and payroll collection, and alert on abnormal request and I/O fill rates.

stride.title: Caller-controlled rota identifiers could grant colleagues or managers access beyond their own scope
stride.description: `process:scheduling-web-app` serves both colleagues viewing their own shifts on `flow:colleague-to-scheduling-web-app:view-shifts` and managers changing a store rota on `flow:store-manager-to-scheduling-web-app:build-rota`; both flows cross from `boundary:public-internet` and have `authentication: unknown`. If the web app or `process:scheduling-service` does not derive the colleague identity and permitted store scope from a verified server-side identity on every request, a legitimate colleague or manager can substitute another colleague or store identifier and cause `flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests` to read or modify resources outside their authority. This is horizontal and potentially vertical authorization escalation through the normal public application surface. Second-order, the scheduling service reads and writes `store:rota-database`, so successful requests can expose or alter rota entries and colleague contact and availability data for other users or stores.

grounds.text: Nobody has documented how colleagues or managers sign in, how the web app and the scheduling service identify each other
Colleague names, contact details and stated availability are held in that database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unverified authentication and authorization design: both attacker populations reach `process:scheduling-web-app` through public-to-internal crossings, and a legitimate colleague or manager need only alter a requested identifier or store scope. Impact is medium because the resulting service request reaches `store:rota-database`, which holds colleague names, contact details, availability, and rota data.

mitigations.summary: Enforce server-side object and store-scope authorization for every rota operation
mitigations.detail: Have `process:scheduling-web-app` and `process:scheduling-service` derive the caller subject and allowed store scope from a verified credential, then deny reads and writes where the requested colleague, rota, or store is outside that scope.

mitigations.summary: Propagate verified caller identity to the scheduling service
mitigations.detail: Authenticate `flow:scheduling-web-app-to-scheduling-service:rota-requests` and propagate a signed, audience-restricted caller context so `process:scheduling-service` can independently enforce ownership and manager role checks rather than trusting caller-supplied identifiers.

mitigations.summary: Add cross-scope authorization regression tests
mitigations.detail: Test that a colleague cannot request another colleague's shifts and that a manager cannot read or modify rotas for a different store, including alternate and newly added routes.
